expectations.text: Opening uses a provocative question or bold claim; doesn't bury the lede
expectations.evidence: Opens with the thesis as a bold one-line claim: 'Most teams should not adopt microservices.' Lede delivered in sentence one.

expectations.text: Major claims backed by numbers/examples from notes; unbackable claims [FILL] or cut
expectations.evidence: Dozen companies/5 years/~2 needed, 8-person/15-service pattern, 40% plumbing, 90% benefit, 20+ engineer threshold all used; anonymized example left as [FILL]; 40% hedged as 'one common pattern from my consulting work'.

expectations.text: Ending includes a concrete next action
expectations.evidence: 'This week, pick one area of your monolith that people are afraid to touch. Draw its real dependencies. Choose one boundary to enforce in code...'

expectations.text: Closes with genuine engagement question, no like-begging
expectations.evidence: 'Where have you seen microservices help a team move faster — or quietly become the product?' — tied to the post's tension; no like/follow requests.
